# Typed timed-call gaps (SIM-009)

The task module runs every positive fixture through the public CLI in both HDL
optimizer modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values. Expected outputs are derived by hand from the
cited clauses, not captured from llg.

| Fixture | Clause and independent oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `local_events` | §§6.17, 6.21, 15.5. Each `initial` block's `x` is its own event: the first wakes at 1, the second at 2. `t(3)` starts at 5 and its branch triggers its own `done` at 8. `t(4)` and `t(5)` run concurrently from 8 with separate events: 12 and 13. `count(2)` starts at 13; its branch reads `n` only in `#n`, increments `hits` at 15 and the task prints at 16. |
| `event_formals` | §§13.5, 15.5. `pick` assigns `e1` to its output after `#1` and prints the record member `q`; `h` names `e1` from time 1, so the trigger at 3 wakes `@h`. `alias_wait` rebinds `h` through its `ref` at 4 while suspended; the trigger of `e2` at 6 wakes `@h`. `swap` starts from `h` (`e2`), wakes on the trigger at 7 and its `e1` is assigned back at return; the trigger of `e1` at 9 wakes `@h`. |
| `event_local_native` | §§9.4.2, 13.5. `t` waits for `posedge l` on its own local, which the detached branch sets at 3: `z 3` (the record formal's string). `down(2)` starts at 3; each activation's branch sets its own `l` 1 later, and the activation then recurses: `down 2 at 4`, `down 1 at 5`, `down 0 at 6`. |
| `recursive_activations` | §§13.3.1, 13.5.2, 15.5. `rec(2)` builds tag `L2`, waits for the trigger at 1, adds 2 to `total` and calls `rec(1)` with its own record (tag `L21`), which waits for 2 and calls `rec(0)` (tag `L210`), which waits for 3 and adds 0. Returns print innermost first, each with its own record and queue: `L210 0 0 3`, `L21 1 10 3`, `L2 2 20 3`; `total` = 2 + 1 + 0 = 3. |
| `static_and_automatic_tasks` | §§6.21, 13.3.1. `t(1)` and `t(2)` share the static `keep`; the second write (2) is what both print after `#2`. `a(3)` and `a(4)` each print their own value. |
| `formal_event_expressions` | §§9.4.2, 13.3.1. Rising `clk` edges are at 1, 3, 5, ...; `addr` becomes 2 at 4 and 3 at 10. `chain(2)` waits for an edge with `addr >= 2` (5), then recurses: `chain(1)` at 7, `chain(0)` at 9. `wait_addr(3, p)` waits for an edge with `addr == 3`: 11, and prints its record member `dev`. |
| `expanded_ref_wakeups` | §§9.4.2, 13.5.2, 9.3.2. `outer`'s branch sets its local at 2, waking `await_edge(loc)` (a typed body since SIM-009-A03; the fixture name records the former expansion): `edge 2`. The block's branch (started at 2) sets `b` at 5: `edge 5`. |
| `expanded_element_refs` | §13.5.2 (typed since SIM-009-A03). The call binds `bus[2]` at 0; `i` = 0 at 1 and `bus[0]` = 1 at 2 do not affect it; `bus[2]` rises at 3: `edge 3`. |
| `expanded_native_qualifiers` | §9.4.2 (typed since SIM-009-A03). `level` rises at 1 and 3 and falls at 2. `gate("go")` resumes at 1 (`go 1`); `gate("stop")`'s qualifier is never true; `gate_null(none)` resumes on the fall at 2: `null 2`. |
| `neg_string_event_control` | Legal by §9.4.2; `@` on a subroutine string has no change marker and is rejected explicitly. |
| `recursive_native_qualifiers` | §§9.4.2, 13.5. `c` rises at 1, 3 and 5; each activation of `r` waits for the next rise, prints and recurses: `x 2 1`, `x 1 3`, `x 0 5`. |
| `ref_level_waits` | §§9.4.3, 13.5.2, 9.3.2. The branch sets `loc` at 1, `flag` to 2 at 2 and 3 at 3, and `arr[1]` at 4; each `wait (r >= v)` resumes when its actual reaches `v`: `level 1 at 1` (the typed body follows the automatic), `level 2 at 2`, `level 3 at 3` (through `forward`), `level 4 at 4` (element, typed since SIM-009-A03). `own(0)` starts at 4; its branch sets the shared formal at 6: `own at 6`. |
| `typed_ref_waits` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.3, 13.5.2. The first branch raises `l` at 1, 3 and 5; `r(l, 2)` waits for a rising edge, prints and recurses with the same variable: `r 2 at 1`, `r 1 at 3`, `r 0 at 5`. `lvl` (with a record formal) starts at 5; `c` becomes 1 at 10 and 3 at 11: `lvl t 3 at 11`. `rl` waits for any change of `x`, set at 20: `real 2.50 at 20`. The last branch (from 20) raises the module signal `g` at 21 and the element `mem[1]` at 22: `r 0 at 21`, `r 0 at 22`. |
| `typed_element_refs` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.3, 13.3.1, 13.5.2 (quotes Q1-Q4, Q6). `carried(u.cells[0], rec, 0)` finds `0` at once: `a 1 0 at 0`; each activation pushes its `n` on its own copy of the record queue, so the later prints show sizes 2 and 3 when `u.cells[0]` becomes 1 (13) and 2 (14). `count(arr[2], 1)`: `arr[2]` = 1 at 1; the store to `arr[1]` at 2 does not satisfy `r >= 2`; 3 at 3 satisfies `count 2` and, at once, `count 3`; 4 at 4 gives `count 4`. `edges(grid[1][2], 1)`: bit 0 goes x to 0 at 5 (no posedge), 0 to 1 at 6 (`edge 1 1`), `grid[1][1]` changes at 7, 1 to 0 at 8, 0 to 1 at 9 (`edge 0 3`). `reals(rs[1], 1)`: 1.5 at 10, `rs[0]` at 11, 2.5 at 12. `c.climb(c.x, 1)`: `x` = 1 at 15, 3 at 16 (`climb 2` and `climb 3`). `outer(2)` at 17 stores each activation's own `la[1]` before `level` waits on it: three prints at 17. |
| `typed_event_lists` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.2.1, 9.4.2.2, 9.4.2.3 (quotes Q2, Q5, Q7, Q13, Q14). `either(loc, "either", 2)`: `ev` at 1; `loc > 1` changes 0 to 1 at 2; at 3 `loc > 0` stays 1 (no event); `ev` at 10. `gated(bits, 1)`: `ev2` at 4; bit 0 rises at 5 with `bits` = 1 (qualifier false), falls at 6, rises at 7 with `bits` = 3. `implicit_list(imp, 1)`: `@*` waits on the variable `r` names; `imp` = 1 at 8 and 2 at 9. |
| `typed_string_handle_refs` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.2.3, 9.4.3, 13.5.2 (quotes Q1-Q4, Q8, Q14). `spell(word, 0)` waits for `w0`, `w1`, `w2` (1, 2, 3). `watch(local_word, 1)`: `a` at 4; writing `a` again at 5 is no change; `b` at 6. `rebound(box, 1)`: a new object at 7; the property store at 8 does not change the handle; `null` at 9 (printed as -1). `member(box2, 0)`: a new object with `v` 0 at 10, `v` = 1 at 11, a new object with `v` 2 at 12. `qualified(word, 0)`: `go` at 13 with `word` = `w2` (qualifier false), `go` at 15 after `word` = `yes` at 14. |
| `container_element_refs` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.3, 13.5.2 (Q1-Q3, Q6). `climb(q[1], 1)`: `q[1]` = 1 at 1 (`climb 1 at 1`); the store to `q[0]` at 2 leaves `r >= 2` false; 2 at 3 (`climb 2 at 3`). `d[1]` = 3 at 5 (after `d[0]` at 4): `dyn 3 at 5`; `aa[5]` = 4 at 7 (after `aa[6]` at 6): `assoc 4 at 7`. `rise(lq[1], 1)`: 0 to 1 at 8, `lq[0]` at 9, 1 to 0 at 10, 0 to 1 at 11. `grow(q, 2)` starts at 12 with size 2; the push at 13 gives size 3 (`grow 3 at 13`); `q[0]` changes from 9 to 4 at 14 (`head 4 at 14`). `shared_wait` (from 14): its branch waits on the shared automatic queue's element, which the other branch sets to 7 at 15. |
| `member_view_refs` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.3, 13.5.2 (Q1-Q3, Q6). `change(us.b, 1)`: `us.a` at 1 is a sibling member; `us.b` = 4 at 2 and 5 at 3. `reach(arr[1].n, 3)`: `arr[0].n` at 4 is another element; 3 at 6. `change(arr[1].p.b, 0)`: `arr[1].p.a` at 5 is a sibling; 9 at 7. `local_member` (from 8): `lp.b` at 9 is a sibling of the bound `lp.a`, which becomes 6 at 10. |
| `aggregate_refs` | §§9.4.3, 13.5.2 (Q1, Q3, Q6). `seek(g, 0)`: `g[0]` = 10 at 1; the activations for 1 and 2 find `g[1]` = 11 at 3 and `g[2]` = 12 at 4 (`g[3]` at 2 satisfies none). `seek(loc, 1)` on the block's automatic array: `loc[1]` = 11 at 5, `loc[2]` = 12 at 7. `total(g, 33)`: the sum is 10, 15, 26, 38 at 1-4 and 33 when `g[3]` returns to 0 at 8. |
| `vif_refs` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.3, 13.5.2, 25.9 (Q1-Q3, Q15). `tick(vi, 2)`: `i0.clk` rises at 1 with `data` 1. After `vi` is rebound to `i1` at 3 the wait follows `i1.clk` (0), so the rise of `i0.clk` at 4 is not seen; `i1.clk` rises at 5 (`data` 5) and, after its fall at 6, at 8 (`data` 7). `settle(vi, 7)`: `i0.data` = 7 at 6 is the old interface; `i1.data` = 7 at 7. |
| `fork_shared_native_refs` | §§9.3.2, 9.4.2, 9.4.3, 13.5.2 (Q1-Q3, Q8, Q16). `owner(7)` shares `s` and `h` with its branches. `spell(s, 2)` recurses twice and waits: `a` at 1, `b` at 3. `held(h, 7)` wakes when the owner stores a new object at 2. The branch waiting for `s == "c"` wakes at 4; the branch on `@(h)`, armed at 2, wakes on the new object at 5. `quiet` (from 6) shares a string no wait observes; its branch's store at 7 is read after the join. |
| `class_property_native_refs` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.3, 13.5.2 (Q1-Q3, Q6, Q8). `word(holder.s, 1)` forwards the property once and waits: `go` at 1, the change to `stop` at 3. `item(holder.item, 1)`: a new object at 2; the property store at 4 does not change the handle; a new object at 5 wakes `@(h)` and the recursive activation finds it non-null at once. |
| `handle_ref_store_wakeups` | §§9.4.2, 13.5.2 (Q1, Q8). `forward(g, 3)` calls `setter`, which stores new objects at 1 and 2: the module waiter prints at each store, before `setter` returns. `setter(root.next, 10)` (from 2) stores at 3 and 4: the property waiter wakes at each. `via_output(g)` (from 4): `make` assigns its output at 5 and the copy-out into the `ref` formal publishes then, while `via_output` still runs until 7. `owner` (from 7): `setter(l, 20)` stores into the shared local at 8 and 9; the branch wakes at each. |
| `fork_visible_element_refs` | §§9.3.2, 9.4.3, 13.5.2 (Q1, Q3, Q6). `store(ia[0], 3)` writes the block's element at 1; the branch writes `ia[1]` at 5; the display at 6 reads both. `owner` (from 6): `await(la[2], 9)` wakes when the detached branch stores 9 at 9; `store(la[0], 4)` wrote at 7; `la[1]` keeps its default 0. |
| `neg_record_ref_wait_actual` | Legal by §§9.4.2, 13.5.2 (Q1, Q2, Q6), but a task waiting on a member of a native record `ref` formal reads leaves that only a module, static or procedural-block record actual binds: a task-automatic record actual is rejected at the call. |
| `neg_native_element_ref_wait` | Legal by §§9.4.2, 13.5.2 (Q1, Q2, Q6), but an element of an unpacked array of strings has no change marker a waiting string `ref` formal can follow: rejected at the call. |
| `neg_function_timing` | Illegal by §13.4 a) (Q9): Slang's located error. |
| `neg_ref_nba` | Illegal by §§13.5.2, 10.4.2 (Q10, Q11): Slang's located error. |
| `neg_automatic_event_capture` | Illegal by §§13.3.2, 13.5.2 (Q10, Q12): Slang's located error. |

## Clause quotes (SIM-009-A03)

Line numbers refer to `SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt` (`pdftotext -layout`).

- Q1, §13.5.2 L19138-19141: "When the argument is passed by reference, both the caller and the subroutine share the same representation of the argument; therefore, any changes made to the argument, within either the caller or the subroutine, shall be visible to each other. The semantics of assignments to variables passed by reference is that changes are seen outside the subroutine immediately (before the subroutine returns)."
- Q2, §9.4.2 L11822-11824: "A variable used with the event control can be any one of the integral data types (see 6.11.1) or string. The variable can be either a simple variable or a ref argument (variable passed by reference); it can be a member of an array, associative array, or object (class instance) of the aforementioned types."
- Q3, §9.4.3 L12032-12033: "The wait statement shall evaluate a condition; and, if it is false, the procedural statements following the wait statement shall remain blocked until that condition becomes true before continuing."
- Q4, §13.3.1 L18621: "All items declared inside automatic tasks are allocated dynamically for each invocation."
- Q5, §9.4.2.2 L11892-11894: "The implicit event_expression, @*, is a convenient shorthand that eliminates these problems by adding all nets and variables that are read by the statement (which can be a statement group) of a procedural_timing_ control_statement to the event_expression."
- Q6, §13.5.2 L19143-19147: "Only the following shall be legal to pass by reference: — a variable, — a class property, — a member of an unpacked structure, or — an element of an unpacked array."
- Q7, §9.4.2 L11772-11773: "A negedge shall be detected on the transition from 1 to x, z, or 0, and from x or z to 0 — A posedge shall be detected on the transition from 0 to x, z, or 1, and from x or z to 1".
- Q8, §9.4.2 L11830-11831: "If the event expression is a reference to a simple object handle or chandle variable, an event is created when a write to that variable is not equal to its previous value."
- Q9, §13.4 L18673-18674: "A function shall not contain any time-controlled statements. That is, any statements containing #, ##, @, fork, wait, wait_order, or expect."
- Q10, §13.5.2 L19151-19152: "Because a variable passed by reference may be an automatic variable, a ref argument shall not be used in any context forbidden for automatic variables."
- Q11, §10.4.2 L13048: "It shall be illegal to make nonblocking assignments to automatic variables."
- Q12, §13.3.2 L18646-18651: "Because variables declared in automatic tasks are deallocated at the end of the task invocation, they shall not be used in certain constructs that might refer to them after that point: [...] They shall not be referenced in intra-assignment event controls of nonblocking assignments."
- Q13, §9.4.2.1 L11870-11871: "The logical or of any number of events can be expressed so that the occurrence of any one of the events triggers the execution of the procedural statement that follows it."
- Q14, §9.4.2.3 L11987-11989: "The event expression only triggers if the expression after the iff is true, in this case when enable is equal to 1. This type of expression is evaluated when a changes and not when enable changes. Also, in similar event expressions of this type, iff has precedence over or."
- Q15, §25.9 L44868: "A virtual interface is a variable that represents an interface instance."
- Q16, §9.3.2 Table 9-1 L11430-11432: "join_none The parent process continues to execute concurrently with all the processes spawned by the fork. The spawned processes do not start executing until the parent thread executes a blocking statement."
